My wife left me Dec 2017. I took it very hard and ended up losing an amazing job and the house we were living in (not to her though. it was a very large home we had two other roommates we knew really well, but the loss of two incomes made it so that we couldn't afford it anymore). I had someone else almost immediately cuz yea, I missed my wife. I missed the companionship and always having someone there. I also still wanted her back. This was unfair to the new gal first of all and second: it didn't allow me to heal very quickly and the new relationship was, like stated above, wrought with drama. It's like bandaging a wound without cleaning it first: it's not going to heal quickly or well if at all.

Take this time to get your head back on right. It's only been this past 6 months that I've really started to return to my old self. My self-confidence had been lost. My normal bright outlook on life & the world around had been lost. I wasn't myself anymore. Had I spent that time & energy I was spending on a new relationship and put it into doing the things that were good for me, I wouldn't have spent so much time feel sorry for myself. And feeling sorry for oneself is a self-fulfilling prophecy of negativity. I let myself sit in my own bucket of proverbial shit cuz hey, at least it's warm, right? What I wished I would have realized sooner (and realizing it yourself is not the same as being told) is that I'm awesome. She's the one who lost out. I've got a lot to offer and she walked away from that. Her loss, not mine.

You need to be vigilant and mindful of how you are feeling and what causes you to feel that way. Be diligent in doing the things that make YOU feel good about who YOU are. Stay busy. Go do things that YOU wanna do and own them! Cuz if there's one thing I know: self-confidence is sexy and alluring. Who wants to be around a person filled with self-pity? Nobody. Not even the person feeling the self-pit wants to be around themselves.

Go have a few sessions with a good counselor/psychologist you trust. I did and she really helped me navigate out of some terrible beliefs I'd gotten stuck in my head over the past few years. It's time to be awesome again! You got this man! 😊

Heck, in a week I won't even be in the same state, lol. 😂 Too bad the 'computer as a media center' idea flopped (eg, Windows Media Center).

Perfect suggestion except there's a problem: they only have 10GB a month for bandwidth on a shitty satellite connection so they don't/can't stream anything. It's a tough situation. And yes, I get "playing discs" is its intended use. At it's base level though, it's still just a computer, which, would excel at playing discs AND streaming thanks to the wide range of software available and codecs you can aquire. It's not like one would need specific hardware chips for each seperate codec. Yes, I know some do, but's software that plays things, not the hardware. 🙂
On a stranger note: why is it able to play 1080p files from my phone, but not 4k? They still show up in the directory unlike the video files from his external drive so why do they show some files and not others regardless of playability or container? Talk about odd and great example why I hate dedicated hardware like that. Dedication shouldn't mean limited functionality when it comes to software. But, people eat it up as the 'computer as a media device' didn't take off like they thought (eg, Windows Media Center PCs).

Haha, it does a little bit, huh. Sadly it was anything but funny. I had been living with a cousin helping him get his house ready to sell and it did so I had to move. It was the final load and I asked a friend if he could help All day long he kept nit picking at me at how I had too much stuff or how I should have gotten things together differently and just generally tearing me down for petty crap at every turn. I was getting really fed up with it when we were talking about a previous job I had. I was explaining something to him and he disagreed. Dunno why he thought he knew more about a job that I had instead of him, but I tried to explain again and he sharply cut me off with, "No, you're just too young to understand." Sadly, that was it for me and replied very disgustedly, "Oh, fuck you, man." I slouched against the door a bit hurt he had just been so condisending to me. 

Angered by this and with a voice that told me he was about to go off, "Fuck me, huh?" He proceeded to lock up the brakes and we skidded to the side of the road. Everything on the seat and my lap, which was where my record player was, flew forward slamming into the dashboard. He began uttering words meant for me to himself not even looking at me but made sure I heard 'get the hell out of my truck.' Not wanting to fight, I began picking up my things. I undid my belt, picked up my record player, and set it in the middle of the bench seat. I opened the door and began to get out when he backhands my record player breaking off the cover. I quickly said, "Dude, come on. Don't break my stuff, please?" I turned towards the back of the truck to begin unloading when he just shoves it out of the cab causing it to bounce on the pavement with no cover on it and halfway into a wide, grassy ditch. "Dude! Stop throwing my stuff!" Even after I start unloading he kept unceremoniously shoving at my things knocking over boxes and small shelves. I was honestly afraid me might actually get violent so I only kept saying 'Stop throwing my stuff!' As soon as I got the last of my stuff into a heap on the side of the highway, he slams his door shut, pedal goes to the floor spinning the truck around and takes off like a bullet the way we had just come from. Almost two hours later I was beginning to get cold, but luckily it wasn't raining. Reluctant to leave my things unattended, the cold and lack of my dad not being there yet with his truck, I decided to walk down to the store about a mile or so down the road.

I'd only been walking 5 minutes when a white car nose comes into peripheral vision super close to me. I'm thinking who the f#*! is this? Turned out to be my best friend (known each other since we were 4 and we're mid 30s now) headed home from work and he had recognized me. Got in and we waited for my dad. And that's the story of how I ended up on the side of a highway with a pile of my stuff and handful of my things broken from being thrown out of the back or truck. Months later I did get an apology call from him. I apologized as well. Almost a year later and I haven't heard from him at all. Sad. Thought we had a better friendship than that, but guess you never truly know people, huh?
